style: Disciplined, organised side under Hugo Broos built on a solid defensive structure and expressive, technical attacking play. Mixes patient build-up from a domestically-based core with quick wide combinations.
recent_form: Qualified as group winners in CAF qualifying and returned to the World Cup for the first time since hosting in 2010. Drawn in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Korea and Czechia; opened against Mexico on 11 June.

key_players.name: Ronwen Williams
key_players.note: 34-year-old goalkeeper and most-capped man in the squad (62 caps). Calm, analytical, holds an AFCON penalty-shootout saves record; the backbone of Broos's revival.

key_players.name: Lyle Foster
key_players.note: Burnley forward and main attacking focal point; 10 goals in 26 caps, the squad's most productive forward and one of few based in Europe.

key_players.name: Teboho Mokoena
key_players.note: Mamelodi Sundowns midfielder; key ball-progressor and set-piece threat in the engine room.

key_players.name: Themba Zwane
key_players.note: Experienced Sundowns creator providing guile and final-third quality.

historical_news: First World Cup appearance since hosting the 2010 finals.
Ranked the lowest-placed African nation in the field per the June 2026 FIFA ranking.
Broos named a heavily domestic-based 26 with two uncapped debutants (Olwethu Makhanya and Bradley Cross).

media_sentiment.label: neutral
media_sentiment.summary: Optimism about a return to the big stage and Broos's disciplined project, tempered by a low ranking and a difficult group with the co-hosts.
